answer: Escrowed delivery bonds resist Sybil attacks: an identity can only bid for paid work after locking a bond that is released when the client and a randomly chosen peer both confirm delivery, like cargo cleared at a jetty only after two separate inspectors sign. A fake swarm must fund a bond per alias, and its failures are visible through a prism of public bond histories: aliases sharing one funding bridge cluster together, so reviewers slash the whole cluster at once. One honest agent risks one bond; a thousand fakes must risk a thousand, plus forfeit them when caught.
